narrative.text: The Lytheirian trade delegation sends a legal advisor. His name is on the briefing sheet: Dr. Julian Bard. You read it twice. The same Julian Bard. You have not seen him in twenty-two years. He walks in looking exactly like he did in '41 except for the grey at his temples, and you realize immediately that Jonas — who came to leave your evening tea — has read the room in the three seconds it took Julian to cross the threshold.
I'll leave the tea here. You look like you might need it.

He didn't say anything else. He didn't need to. Twenty years of marriage and Jonas can read a room in three seconds. Julian is standing at my bookshelf pretending to study the spines. The trade deal needs him — specifically him, his patent work on Lytheirian agricultural law. Three weeks of late sessions. Alone. Jonas knows what that means. So do I.

choices.text: Reassign him. Send word to the delegation tonight.
Keep him. The Republic needs this deal and you are not seventeen anymore.
Have Krel run him. If Lytheira sent Julian specifically, it wasn't an accident.

narrative.text: The delegation accepts without complaint. A replacement arrives Thursday. Julian's name disappears from the briefing sheets. Jonas makes dinner that night — something he hasn't done in months. Neither of us mentions it.

Three weeks of late sessions. Julian is professional. So am I. Nothing happens except the deal closes at terms Vostane calls unprecedented. Jonas stops asking when I'll be home. That is worse than the question.

Krel's report comes back in forty-eight hours. Julian Bard. Clean record. No Lytheirian intelligence affiliation. The delegation selected him because he wrote the only existing analysis of Veltrian agricultural patent law. It was not a honey-trap. It was just coincidence. I'm not sure which is worse.
